attribution.note: Marcus's own words on his Substack, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: A present-tense observation. The draft says 'AI researchers' where Marcus wrote 'researchers', and 'serious' where he wrote 'huge'. Both are small changes, and the contract scores on the broader 'researchers' wording.

contract.note: Counting disagreement that current LLMs are intelligent as substantive doubt is an ordinary reading of 'huge doubts about LLMs'. The contract flags that this step is the evaluator's interpretation. Setting 'hundreds' at 200 or more is a fair minimum.

evidence.note: Sutskever's Nov 2025 interview says models generalize dramatically worse than people. That is a substantial doubt about current LLMs.
Sutton's Sep 2025 interview rejects the LLM framework's basis for knowledge and ground truth. That clearly counts as substantial doubt.
Peer-reviewed survey: about 71% of 300 Q8 respondents disagreed that current systems are intelligent, roughly 213 people. That clears 200 even allowing for rounding.
This is Marcus's own interview statement, so it cannot prove his claim about himself. His doubts are not really in dispute anyway.

reviews.rationale: Original interviews show substantial doubts about LLMs from both Sutskever and Sutton. A primary survey shows about 213 researchers rejecting the view that current systems are intelligent, which meets the 200 threshold on the contract's fair plain reading. Marcus's own part is self-report and is not needed. Remaining caveat: the survey dates from January 2025.

attribution.note: Marcus's own assessment in his own post. The quoted Denis O. text comes after it and is not part of this claim.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the full description of LeCun's JEPA world models: opaque, uninterpretable, and not suited to reasoning. The claim is evaluative but makes testable architectural assertions.

contract.note: Narrowing 'reasoning' to formal reasoning over structured knowledge follows Marcus's own surrounding text. Treating 'doesn't lend itself' as poor suitability rather than impossibility is a fair ordinary reading.

evidence.note: The V-JEPA 2 paper confirms a neural ViT architecture. It contains no formal-reasoning test and no faithful interpretability analysis. Decoding predictions into frames qualifies 'uninterpretable' only weakly.
Meta's description of its own work shows image-goal robot planning. That does not settle formal reasoning either way.
Text-JEPA is another team's system with an added symbolic solver. It is a different implementation and cannot settle the claim about LeCun's system.

reviews.rationale: None of the evidence directly evaluates whether LeCun's JEPA implementations are interpretable or suited to formal reasoning over structured knowledge. The architecture is neural, and the planning demos fall outside the contract's scope. With no evidence either way, the packet does not settle the claim.
